newsitem.title: ITALY: International Red Cross wins major peace award.
newsitem.headline: International Red Cross wins major peace award.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross was on Wednesday awarded a prestigious Italian-Swiss prize of one million Swiss francs ($800,000) for services to peace, specifically for its work in hospitals in Afghanistan.
The prize, funded by the International Balzan Foundation based in Switzerland and Italy, is awarded only once every three years for humanity, peace and brotherhood amongst peoples.

The foundation said in a statement from its Milan office it had given the ICRC the prize for its work in "the hospitals of Wazir Akbar Khan and Karte Seh in Kabul, Afghanistan, for the physical rehabilitation and re-education programmes for war victims, above all those of antipersonnel landmines."

"The International Committee of the Red Cross is the only organisation which has remained active in Afghanistan during all the wars fought there. Presently they are furnishing the assistance of experts and autonomously running four hospitals. In the hospital of Wazir Akbar Khan in Kabul alone, they have reached the level of performing up to 60 amputations a day," the statement added.
The Balzan Foundation also announced the names of three winners of an annual 500,000 Swiss franc ($403,000) prize, awarded this year in the scientific and humanistic fields.

It named the winners as Arnt Eliassen of Norway for Meteorology, American Stanley Hoffmann for Political Science: contemporary international relations, and Arno Borst of Germany for History: mediaeval culture.
The foundation was established in Lugano, Switzerland, in 1956 by the daughter of the late Italian journalist Eugenio Balzan, whose inheritance is used to fund the awards.
The award-giving ceremony will take place in Rome on November 19 in the presence of Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
The foundation said next year's awards would be in the fields of epidemiology, social anthropology and the history and philosophy of science.
